items.statement: GM U.S. consumer revenue is 45% to 65% of consolidated revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: GM reports U.S. sales and GM Financial U.S. retail-sales penetration.
items.sensitivity_note: A lower U.S.-consumer share raises GM's estimated DFR percentage.

items.statement: Ford U.S. consumer revenue is 45% to 65% of consolidated revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: Ford reports 2,204,124 U.S. vehicle sales for 2025.
items.sensitivity_note: A lower U.S.-consumer share raises Ford's estimated DFR percentage.

items.statement: Amazon U.S. consumer revenue is 45% to 60% of consolidated revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: North America, International, and AWS are separately disclosed reportable segments.
items.sensitivity_note: The split between U.S. consumer activity and AWS/international revenue dominates the denominator.

items.statement: Walmart U.S. consumer revenue is 68% to 76% of consolidated revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: Walmart U.S., Walmart International, and Sam's Club U.S. are separately reported.
items.sensitivity_note: The modeled U.S. share moves Walmart's denominator and aggregate index weight.

items.statement: Target U.S. consumer revenue is 98% to 100% of consolidated revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: Nearly all of our sales are in the U.S.
items.sensitivity_note: Target's disclosed U.S. concentration makes this a narrow denominator prior.

items.statement: Lowe's U.S. consumer revenue is 82% to 96% of consolidated revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: Lowe's operated 1,759 stores and outlets in the United States.
items.sensitivity_note: The range excludes modeled Canadian and professional-customer activity from consumer revenue.

items.statement: Home Depot U.S. consumer revenue is 75% to 90% of consolidated revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: The filing separates U.S. retail activity from Canada, Mexico, and professional distribution.
items.sensitivity_note: The consumer/professional split is the largest Home Depot denominator uncertainty.

items.statement: Best Buy U.S. consumer revenue is 80% to 94% of consolidated revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: Best Buy separately reports Domestic and International segment revenue.
items.sensitivity_note: The prior removes international and modeled non-consumer revenue from the denominator.

items.statement: Ulta U.S. consumer revenue is 90% to 98% of consolidated revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: Ulta has one reportable retail, salon, and e-commerce segment.
items.sensitivity_note: The range allows for non-U.S. and non-consumer revenue without treating it as observed.

items.statement: Tractor Supply U.S. consumer revenue is 86% to 97% of consolidated revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: The filing describes U.S. retail sales and tax-exempt agricultural customers.
items.sensitivity_note: The range removes modeled business and tax-exempt agricultural sales from consumer revenue.

items.statement: GM receives 8% to 14% of national nonrevolving flow through its captive-linked sales channel.
items.evidence_snippet: GM Financial's penetration of our retail sales in the U.S. was 33%.
items.sensitivity_note: This converts observed captive penetration into a share of national nonrevolving flow.

items.statement: Ford receives 7% to 14% of national nonrevolving flow through its captive-linked sales channel.
items.evidence_snippet: The predominant share of Ford Credit's business consists of financing our vehicles.
items.sensitivity_note: Current financing share is not disclosed; the wide prior is anchored to captive activity.

items.statement: Amazon-linked branded cards and promotional financing receive 1% to 4% of revolving flow.
items.evidence_snippet: We also offer co-branded credit card programs.
items.sensitivity_note: Amazon does not disclose program purchase volume; this allocation remains wide.

items.statement: Walmart-linked cards and installment lending receive 0.4% to 1.5% of revolving flow.
items.evidence_snippet: co-branded credit cards, limited access to cryptocurrency and equity investment products, installment lending
items.sensitivity_note: The new program lacks a disclosed purchase-volume history, so the allocation is conservative.

items.statement: Target Circle cards receive 0.3% to 1.0% of national revolving flow.
items.evidence_snippet: total Target Circle Card Penetration was 16.9 percent
items.sensitivity_note: Observed store penetration is converted into an uncertain national-flow share.

items.statement: Lowe's branded cards receive 0.3% to 1.2% of national revolving flow.
items.evidence_snippet: branded and private label proprietary credit cards which generate sales
items.sensitivity_note: No purchase-volume percentage is disclosed; the program allocation is modeled.

items.statement: Home Depot credit programs receive 0.4% to 1.5% of national revolving flow.
items.evidence_snippet: third-party service providers who directly extend credit to customers
items.sensitivity_note: Program volume is not disclosed and therefore remains a wide prior.

items.statement: Best Buy branded cards receive 0.2% to 1.0% of national revolving flow.
items.evidence_snippet: We facilitate credit applications in our stores and online.
items.sensitivity_note: The filing links the program to purchases but does not disclose purchase volume.

items.statement: Ulta branded cards receive 0.05% to 0.4% of national revolving flow.
items.evidence_snippet: Other revenue includes private label and co-branded credit card programs.
items.sensitivity_note: Program volume is not disclosed; the range scales to Ulta's revenue footprint.

items.statement: Tractor Supply private-label cards receive 0.05% to 0.4% of national revolving flow.
items.evidence_snippet: Sales generated through the Company's private label credit cards
items.sensitivity_note: Program volume is not disclosed; the range scales to Tractor Supply's footprint.

items.statement: General retail receives 22% to 42% of national revolving-credit flow.
items.evidence_snippet: MARTS publishes monthly retail sales by kind of business.
items.sensitivity_note: This is the main Tier 2 category-mapping uncertainty for retailers.

items.statement: Covered auto sales receive 8% to 18% of national nonrevolving-credit flow.
items.evidence_snippet: Household Debt and Credit reports auto-loan balances and originations.
items.sensitivity_note: Nonrevolving credit includes education and other loans, so the auto share is uncertain.

items.statement: Six to fourteen percent of revolving flow is fungibly allocated to covered consumer revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: BEA publishes monthly personal consumption expenditures by type.
items.sensitivity_note: This widest-tier allocation tests unassignable revolving-credit use.

items.statement: Six to fourteen percent of nonrevolving flow is fungibly allocated to covered consumer revenue.
items.evidence_snippet: BEA publishes monthly personal consumption expenditures by type.
items.sensitivity_note: This widest-tier allocation captures personal and otherwise unassignable loans.

items.statement: Amazon receives 10% to 22% of the covered general-retail allocation.
items.evidence_snippet: Amazon reports North America retail sales and third-party seller services.
items.sensitivity_note: Marketplace gross sales are not consolidated revenue, widening category share.

items.statement: Walmart receives 15% to 28% of the covered general-retail allocation.
items.evidence_snippet: Walmart reports U.S. and Sam's Club U.S. net sales.
items.sensitivity_note: Grocery and non-consumer components create the category-share range.

items.statement: Target receives 4% to 9% of the covered general-retail allocation.
items.evidence_snippet: Target reports merchandise sales across six consumer categories.
items.sensitivity_note: Food and household-essential mix changes its relevant general-retail share.

items.statement: Lowe's receives 2% to 7% of the covered general-retail allocation.
items.evidence_snippet: Lowe's reports home-improvement retail net sales.
items.sensitivity_note: Professional sales are removed through the denominator and category priors.

items.statement: Home Depot receives 3% to 8% of the covered general-retail allocation.
items.evidence_snippet: Home Depot reports retail and professional-customer net sales.
items.sensitivity_note: Professional distribution makes the consumer category share uncertain.

items.statement: Best Buy receives 1.5% to 4% of the covered general-retail allocation.
items.evidence_snippet: Best Buy reports Domestic consumer-electronics revenue.
items.sensitivity_note: The range reflects overlap between electronics and general retail.

items.statement: Ulta receives 0.5% to 2% of the covered general-retail allocation.
items.evidence_snippet: Ulta reports retail, salon, and e-commerce revenue.
items.sensitivity_note: Beauty is a narrow subset of general retail.

items.statement: Tractor Supply receives 0.5% to 2% of the covered general-retail allocation.
items.evidence_snippet: Tractor Supply reports consumer and agricultural retail sales.
items.sensitivity_note: Agricultural-business purchases broaden the category-share range.

items.statement: GM receives 8% to 16% of the remaining covered auto allocation.
items.evidence_snippet: GM reports U.S. vehicle sales and market share.
items.sensitivity_note: Manufacturer revenue does not equal dealer retail receipts, so the share is banded.

items.statement: Ford receives 8% to 16% of the remaining covered auto allocation.
items.evidence_snippet: Ford reports U.S. vehicle sales and market share.
items.sensitivity_note: Manufacturer revenue does not equal dealer retail receipts, so the share is banded.
